startingDetails.title: Main destination markets

startingDetails.title: Expected order volume
startingDetails.copy: A rough daily range helps us recommend the right warehouse and fulfillment setup.

startingDetails.title: Branding/QC needs
startingDetails.copy: Send packaging, label and inspection notes before dispatch.

stages.title: Share your product
stages.intro: Send one clear product reference so the first conversation stays focused on your actual store and customer promise.
stages.provide: Product link, target market, expected volume and the problem you want to solve.
stages.handle: Review product feasibility, service scope, destination requirements and missing information.
stages.receive: A focused product brief and a clear recommendation for the next step.

stages.title: Source and quote
stages.intro: Suitable supplier offers are compared on the same specification, not only on the lowest unit price.
stages.provide: Target cost, material or feature requirements, quantity and desired launch timing.
stages.handle: Compare suppliers, MOQ, lead time, customization, packaging and estimated fulfillment implications.
stages.receive: Comparable options with the trade-offs needed to make a supplier decision.

stages.title: Sample and approve
stages.intro: The physical product and its inspection scope are agreed before repeat purchasing or daily fulfillment begins.
stages.provide: Feedback on the sample, acceptable tolerances and any non-negotiable brand details.
stages.handle: Coordinate samples, review visible quality, confirm variants, packaging and QC checkpoints.
stages.receive: An approved reference and a documented basis for future product checks.

stages.title: Set up fulfillment
stages.intro: Inventory, SKUs, packaging materials and order rules are connected before live customer volume is released.
stages.provide: Store SKU data, packing instructions, branding files and order handoff preference.
stages.handle: Receive stock, map variants, prepare storage, document packing rules and run test orders.
stages.receive: A tested order workflow ready for repeat picking, checking and packing.

stages.title: Ship and sync tracking
stages.intro: Approved orders move through dispatch while shipment status and exceptions remain visible to your team.
stages.provide: Customer orders, addresses and the agreed shipping or service-level rules.
stages.handle: Pick, final-check, pack, label, dispatch and separate orders that require a decision.
stages.receive: Shipment confirmation, carrier details and tracking through the agreed handoff.

checkpoints: Supplier terms, specification and sample plan confirmed.
SKU, quantity, packaging and inbound expectations documented.
Product, variant, parcel and label checked against the order.
faqs: Timing depends on the product, sample work, packaging and stock readiness. After the first review, we identify the stages that apply and the dependencies that control launch timing.
Can I start before my store has daily orders?
Yes. Product sourcing, supplier comparison and samples can begin before launch. The fulfillment setup can then be prepared when products and expected order flow are clearer.
Can JW work with my existing supplier?
Yes. Your supplier can send inventory to the JW warehouse while we focus on receiving, quality checks, storage, packing and global dispatch.
What happens when a quality issue is found?
Affected goods or orders can be held, documented and shared for your decision. The exact inspection and approval process is agreed before operations begin.
How do orders and tracking move between our teams?
The handoff may use a supported store workflow, structured order file or another agreed method. SKU mapping and exception rules are confirmed during setup.
